newsitem.title: USA: Global corporate bond issuers lead action in U.S..
newsitem.headline: Global corporate bond issuers lead action in U.S..

text.p: Large global offerings of corporate bonds were making waves on Wall Street on Wednesday in what is otherwise likely to be a slow week for new corporate bond issuance, market players said.
"Right now, at these interest rate levels, it's compelling for larger global issuers to hit the market," said one syndicate official.

Sakura Bank, the third largest bank in Japan, is preparing a $1 billion offering of subordinated guaranteed perpetual bonds which will be marketed to both 144a investors in the U.S. and Eurobond investors.
Merrill Lynch & Co will be the sole underwriter for the offering which is expected to price later this week.
Ford Motor Credit Corp, the finance subsidiary of Ford Motor Co, is also pricing a $1 billion global offering this week that will be sold in the U.S., Europe and Asia.
Goldman Sachs & Co and Salomon Brothers Inc are co-lead managing the deal.
"The Ford deal appears to be in very good shape. It has been marketed way in advance of the offering," said one synidcate official from a competing investment bank.
Market players said large corporations are increasingly "globalizing" their offerings of dollar-deonominated bonds in order to tap stronger worldwide demand.
An important reason for this is the strength of the dollar, which has increased thirst for dollar-denominated investments from investors around the world, they said.

Another factor at work is the development of U.S.-style corporate bond markets in many countries, particularly in Europe, they said. London and Frankfurt have become centers for corporate bond trading in Europe, they noted.
The Sakura Bank offering was structured with two separate tranches in order to target different investor groups around the world, market sources said.

The first tranche has a fixed-rate coupon for five years and subsequently converts into a floating rate bond. The structure is designed to appeal to U.S. investors who prefer investing in fixed-rate securities, syndicate sources said.
The second tranche, designed for European investors, is purely a floating rate security, they said.
The bonds are being sold by Sakura Capital Funding Ltd, a finance subsidiary of Sakura Bank, and are rated Baa2/BBB.
Elsewhere in the high-grade market, software maker, Oracle Corp is expected to price $300 million in seven and 10-year bonds via Morgan Stanley & Co on Wednesday afternoon, syndicate officials said.
